data.title: Everolimus plus exemestane for hormone-receptor-positive, human epidermal growth factor receptor-2-negative advanced breast cancer: overall survival results from BOLERO-2†
data.authors: Piccart M; Hortobagyi GN; Campone M; Pritchard KI; Lebrun F; Ito Y; Noguchi S; Perez A; Rugo HS; Deleu I; Burris HA; Provencher L; Neven P; Gnant M; Shtivelband M; Wu C; Fan J; Feng W; Taran T; Baselga J

evidence.label: Human study
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

data.model_system: Humans: postmenopausal women with HR+/HER2- advanced breast cancer after nonsteroidal aromatase inhibitors; phase III RCT, everolimus + exemestane vs placebo + exemestane (2:1)
data.finding: This is the final overall-survival report of BOLERO-2, the phase III double-blind trial (published primary analysis: BAS2012) in which postmenopausal women with hormone-receptor-positive, HER2-negative advanced breast cancer that had progressed on a nonsteroidal aromatase inhibitor received exemestane 25 mg/day plus either everolimus 10 mg/day or placebo. The primary endpoint, progression-free survival by local investigator, remained improved: median 7.8 vs 3.2 months (P < 0.0001), a 4.6-month gain. Overall survival, a key secondary endpoint, was not significantly improved: median 31.0 vs 26.6 months, hazard ratio 0.89 (95% CI 0.73-1.10), P = 0.14, at 410 deaths. Most patients went on to further treatment after the trial (84% vs 90%), with less chemotherapy in the everolimus arm (53% vs 63%), which may have diluted any survival difference. No new safety concerns were identified. Boundary: postmenopausal women with HR+/HER2- advanced breast cancer previously treated with a nonsteroidal aromatase inhibitor; comparator was exemestane plus placebo; the survival benefit of adding mTOR inhibition was not shown.
data.abstract_excerpt: The BOLERO-2 study previously demonstrated that adding everolimus (EVE) to exemestane (EXE) significantly improved progression-free survival (PFS) by more than twofold in patients with hormone-receptor-positive (HR(+)), HER2-negative advanced breast cancer that recurred or progressed during/after treatment with nonsteroidal aromatase inhibitors (NSAIs). The overall survival (OS) analysis is presented here.

extracted_findings.intervention: Everolimus 10 mg/day + exemestane 25 mg/day vs placebo + exemestane
extracted_findings.effect: PFS improved (7.8 vs 3.2 mo); overall survival not significantly improved (HR 0.89, P = 0.14)
